title: Marcus Scribonius Libo Drusus Accused of Magic; Suicide
description: Marcus Scribonius Libo Drusus was accused in 16 CE of consulting astrologers and magicians to determine whether he would become emperor, combining charges of veneficium with maiestas (treason). Tacitus records that he had consulted a Chaldean astrologer named Firmius Catus and that magical writings were found attributed to him. Faced with certain conviction, Libo Drusus killed himself before the Senate could render judgment. His case was an early and prominent example of the Tiberian pattern of using magic accusations as political weapons, and his posthumous condemnation set precedents for subsequent prosecutions.
historiographical_note: This case has been analyzed within the broader scholarship on Tiberian repression (Seager, Levick) as an early instance of the toxic combination of magic and treason charges that would characterize subsequent political prosecutions.
